outer_envelope_definitions.text: quant #outer [[contract]] rk_plugin_library, "every library named by plugin.library.paths, including code it invokes, registers rk_conf callbacks only through public setters and only when each callback meets that member's candidate contract; it registers interceptors only through the public setters, with success result zero and each exact list/union-arm candidate in outer-candidates:5c3f8c4723832c0e9e6ebb784be6a57ebc0264d519421d5b95a18a8f68c18147; every registered interceptor and all code it invokes meets that inventory's neutral custody restriction (all pointer arguments borrowed, no release, retention, ownership transfer or global custody effects, scalar resource handles borrowed too, and every local acquisition balanced before return); registered callback code and opaque contexts remain valid through the last possible invocation, including destruction and copied on_new registrations; configuration interceptors are installed on a live configuration and client interceptors only from on_new before initialization completes, never on share consumers; it calls cJSON_InitHooks nowhere and does not replace cJSON's global allocator hooks; it neither mutates cJSON child, prev or next links directly nor passes malformed cJSON lists to an API call; it never directly stores into librdkafka internal members (including callback fields, op fields, broker and rule-14t links, queues and list links); it invokes no non-public librdkafka symbol and calls public APIs only under their published conditions; any allocator hooks installed before this library loads satisfy cjson_allocator_hooks";

quant #outer [[contract]] flb_external_plugin, "every Fluent Bit plugin loaded from outside the build (a C shared object through flb_plugin_load or a Go plugin through flb_plugin_proxy_create), including code it invokes, stores into no core-owned flb_*_instance or flb_config member; it reaches only handed objects and exported APIs and forges no pointer; when it uses librdkafka it registers rk_conf callbacks only through public setters and only when each callback meets that member's candidate contract, registers interceptors only through public setters, never directly stores into librdkafka internal members (including callback fields, op fields, broker and rule-14t links, queues and list links), invokes no non-public librdkafka symbol, and calls public APIs only under their published conditions; it calls cJSON_InitHooks nowhere and does not replace cJSON's global allocator hooks, neither mutates cJSON child, prev or next links directly nor passes malformed cJSON lists to an API call, and any allocator hooks installed before it loads satisfy cjson_allocator_hooks; every interceptor registration uses the public setter with success result zero and the exact list/union-arm candidate in outer-candidates:5c3f8c4723832c0e9e6ebb784be6a57ebc0264d519421d5b95a18a8f68c18147; every registered interceptor and its transitive calls meets the neutral custody restriction (all pointer arguments borrowed, no release, retention, ownership transfer or global custody effects, scalar resource handles borrowed too, and every local acquisition balanced before return); registered callback code and opaque contexts remain valid through the last possible invocation, including destruction and copied on_new registrations; configuration interceptors are installed on a live configuration and client interceptors only from on_new before initialization completes, never on share consumers";
